hiatus.name: Hiatus tracker
hiatus.metaTitle: Hunter x Hunter hiatus history: every major break since 1998
hiatus.metaDescription: Live count of the current HUNTER×HUNTER hiatus and the full record of {count} breaks of {threshold} Jump issues or more since 1998, measured from Weekly Shonen Jump's own issue numbering.
hiatus.lede: See the current pause, then past pauses lasting at least ten Jump issues. Dates show elapsed time; issue counts show how many published magazines had no chapter.
hiatus.historyTitle: Every hiatus of {threshold} issues or more
hiatus.historyIntro: {count} breaks of at least {threshold} Jump issues are recorded in the dataset. The longest ran {max} issues.
hiatus.methodTitle: How a hiatus is counted here
hiatus.methodBody: A Jump issue that carries no HUNTER×HUNTER chapter counts as one issue of hiatus. Combined issues count once, which is how Shueisha numbers them. Nothing here is an estimate: every issue in the dataset is a published Weekly Shonen Jump issue between 1998 and today.

about.name: About
about.metaTitle: About HxH Status: what it tracks, where the data comes from, and who runs it
about.metaDescription: An unofficial, open-source Hunter x Hunter tracker: sourced production status, publication history and a clearly labelled statistical return estimate.
about.lede: An unofficial, open-source Hunter x Hunter tracker: sourced production status, publication history and a clearly labelled statistical return estimate.
about.rule1: Nothing is recorded without a public source: a post by Yoshihiro Togashi, or an announcement by Weekly Shonen Jump or Shueisha.
about.rule2: Official dates and statistical estimates are kept separate. The next-chapter page may show an explicitly labelled historical estimate, with its method, uncertainty and past errors.
about.rule3: The site and public API use the same recorded data.
about.rule4: Changes are public: anyone can review the correction history.
about.sourcesBody: Yoshihiro Togashi's own posts, Weekly Shonen Jump, Shueisha's official readers, and the Weekly Shonen Jump issue index from 1998 to today.
about.correctionsBody: Found a wrong date or missing source? Report it on GitHub with a link to the evidence. Previous changes remain available in the public history.
about.whoBody: One contributor maintains HxH Status, with translations contributed by readers. The code and data are public on GitHub.
about.creditsBody: The publication history in this tracker is derived from the HUNTER×HUNTER Hiatus Chart by hiatus-hiatus and its contributors, used under the MIT License.

api.name: API
api.metaTitle: HxH Status public API: free HUNTER×HUNTER status JSON, feeds and badges
api.metaDescription: A free, key-less, CORS-enabled JSON API for HUNTER×HUNTER publication status, hiatus statistics and Togashi's translated posts, plus Atom feeds, an iCalendar of releases and embeddable SVG badges.
api.lede: Everything HxH Status knows is served as JSON. No key, no rate limit beyond ordinary caching, CORS open to any origin, and a stable schema version on every document.
api.badgeBody: Embed the current status in a README or a fan site. The image is regenerated whenever the tracker changes.
api.openApiBody: An OpenAPI 3.1 document describes every endpoint above.
api.cachingBody: Every document carries an ETag and a five-minute cache policy, and each response names a pollAfterSeconds value. Please respect it: the tracker changes a few times a month, not a few times a minute.
api.attributionBody: Use of the API is free. A link back to hxhstatus.com is appreciated and helps other readers find the source.

forecast.badge: Model estimate · not an official date
forecast.title: When could chapter {chapter} return?
forecast.intro: Two exploratory models: historical interruptions and a scenario informed by Togashi’s manuscript reports. Probabilities depend on their assumptions.
forecast.asOf: Calculated {date} · {total} interruptions, {count} with exact calendar dates.
forecast.caution: 80% probability within a model does not establish 80% real-world reliability. Data are sparse and editorial decisions remain unknown.
forecast.method: Historical reference: every completed interruption since 2014 between consecutive numbered chapters, including short breaks. Duration runs from the last chapter to the return. Exact dates take precedence; otherwise assume 48 Jump issues per year.
forecast.conditioning: Log duration is normally distributed. A normal–inverse-gamma prior represents uncertainty in its mean and variance. Integrating both yields a Student-t predictive distribution, conditioned on no return by the calculation date. Recomputed at each site build.
forecast.limits: Short and long interruptions are heterogeneous; one distribution cannot describe every regime change. The 2014 cutoff and issue-to-day conversion are assumptions, not learned parameters. No medical information is inferred from posts. An official date hides these estimates.
forecast.sensitivity: Using eligible history since 1998 gives a median of {date}.
forecast.backtest: Chronological validation on {count} returns: mean absolute error {days} days; {covered}/{count} inside the 80% interval. Each prediction uses only previously completed interruptions.
forecast.sampleTitle: Completed breaks used by the model
forecast.unavailable: Insufficient data to calculate this estimate.
forecast.productionBody: Assumption: Jump waits for ten finished manuscripts, then an editorial delay. This is not an announced rule. {count}/10 are confirmed; {remaining} have no completion announcement.
forecast.productionMethod: Announcement rate: Poisson process with a Gamma(1, 30) prior in days. Time without a new announcement is included. The delay after the tenth manuscript uses another Bayesian log-normal model: only {count} usable historical cycle, so strong prior dependence and no out-of-sample validation of this scenario. Reports may be delayed or incomplete.
forecast.probabilityTitle: Modelled probability of return within the next…
forecast.curveTitle: Cumulative probability from the calculation date
forecast.priorBody: The historical prior centers log(T) on log(365.2425 days), with κ₀ = 0.25, α₀ = 2 and β₀ = 1. Centering on 180 or 730 days instead gives medians of {early} and {late}.
forecast.scores: Comparison with a fitted log-normal without parameter uncertainty: error {baseline} days. Mean log score: Bayes {bayes}, reference {score} (higher is better). So few returns cannot establish superiority.
forecast.lagEvidence: Reference cycle: chapter {chapter}, batch completed {completed}, return {released} — {days} days.
forecast.lagSensitivity: Centering the editorial-delay prior on 30 or 180 days instead of 90 moves the scenario median to {early} or {late}.
forecast.centralExplanation: This is the middle of the model’s distribution: half the probability is before this point, half after. It does not predict that exact day.
forecast.clearRange: According to the model, there is a {percent} chance of release between {start} and {end}.
forecast.simpleCaution: These are uncertain model probabilities, not measured reliability. Only the publisher can confirm a date; a finished manuscript does not set the release schedule.
forecast.monthsExplanation: Chance of release during each month, ranked from highest to lowest. Other months includes all remaining dates; rounded values total 100%.
forecast.whyTitle: What this estimate is based on
forecast.simpleProduction: Togashi has confirmed {count} finished manuscripts in the next batch; {remaining} are still unconfirmed. This scenario assumes ten completed manuscripts, then an editorial wait. That is not an announced rule, and only one past cycle informs the editorial delay.
forecast.simpleHistory: This estimate uses past pauses and the time already elapsed without a return. It cannot account for unannounced editorial decisions.
